steps.content: In your stuffy office where the air hangs heavy and still, you silently leaf through a medical report about Wuhuanzi's patients.
As you read on, your brow furrows in confusion. You're reading the words, but you're not understanding anything.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Drinking water mixed with paper talisman ashes, sticking talismans on people's bodies, making patients dig up weeds, acupuncture... These treatment methods sure seem familiar to you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After what happened at the fete, nothing surprises me anymore.
Nightingale gives a slight smile as you turn the pages, coming across the patients' latest physical examination results.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The Bureau arranged medical examinations for these patients, and well... They're all in good shape. Healthier than before, even.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Eastian medicine... is truly beyond our understanding.
You stroke your chin thoughtfully, setting aside your doubts for now as you pick up another report—this one tracking her movements.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: After entering DisCity, Wuhuanzi ran street clinics in crowded areas. Despite her low fees, she attracted few patients. She would also often get driven away by security officers for practicing without a license.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's understandable that DisCity residents would be wary of such a young traveling doctor claiming to be from Eastia.
Even if her skills are genuine, those treatment methods would scare quite a few people away. You add inwardly while unconsciously checking for nonexistent acupuncture marks on your body.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Eventually she reached the Drifter Camp and stayed there for a while before continuing her medical practice elsewhere, until she got involved in the Wisteria Mania incident. After that, she remained there offering free medical services. For good karma, she said.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...For <color=#fb9259>good karma</color>.
She kept mentioning this word during the fete too. What exactly does good karma mean? You were too busy recovering your Qi to ask back then, but perhaps now is a good time to find out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Has she shown any changes since joining the Bureau?
Nightingale shakes her head and looks up from her device.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Since joining the Bureau, she's been proactively offering treatment to both Sinners and staff members. She's not offended when they refuse either. She simply returns after some time and offers her service again like it's some kind of routine check-up.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, Wuhuanzi's Interrogation is scheduled for two days from now. Do we need more time for observation? Also, should we stop her from providing unauthorized medical treatment within the Bureau?

Instead of answering Nightingale right away, you tap your fingers thoughtfully on the desk. While Wuhuanzi's behavior seems consistent with her pattern since her arrival in DisCity, something about it feels off.
According to these two reports, Wuhuanzi never stays in one place for too long, and she appears to show no interest in following up on her patients' conditions.
Just like at the Bureau, patients everywhere are often skeptical and refuse her treatment. But rather than showing any frustration, she simply moves on to the next potential patient.

Day after day, she lives this life of constant rejection and suspicion, showing neither desire nor initiative. You begin to wonder if her medical practice is just another part of her well-programmed routine.
Rather than curing her patients thoroughly, Wuhuanzi seems more concerned with treating as many people as possible. Almost as if she's trying to... meet some kind of performance quota.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No need. We'll proceed with the interrogation as scheduled. As for how to handle her unauthorized medical practice, the interrogation should give us our answers.
In the interrogation room, the petite Eastian girl sits stiffly in her chair.
She takes a brief glance around the claustrophobic room, showing neither panic nor anxiety. Instead, she sits in silence, waiting for your arrival.
You turn on the light. Due to a faulty connection, it flickers several times before finally staying on.
Wuhuanzi instinctively raises her hand to shield her eyes. Realizing the light isn't as harsh as she expected, she slowly lowers it.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Phew, that's a relief... I thought this would be the fifth light I would have broken since coming to the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Relax. The Bureau's equipment is sturdier than that.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: My friend, your complexion has worsened during the days I didn't see you. Ashen face, furrowed brow, lifeless eyes, pale lips...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Did you bring me to this private cell today so I could give you a special consultation?
Her eyes are largely hidden behind thick bangs, making her expression unreadable, but in her quiet muttering, you detect some sort of... enthusiasm?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: One must never turn a blind eye to their ailments, however mild they might be. As fortune would have it, I wrote a new healing talisman just yesterday...

Wuhuanzi leans forward and pulls a bright yellow talisman from her wide sleeve. You wave your hands frantically in refusal, terrified that she might burn it into ashes and force you to drink them any second now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm in reasonably good health, thank you.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...Very well, you can come to me for treatment whenever you need it.
Wuhuanzi looks unbothered. Seemingly used to this kind of response, she tucks the talisman back into her sleeve and meticulously straightens the cuff.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Eastian medicine focuses on observing one's vital energy, predicting its course, and treating ailments before they manifest. It's simply a different approach from DisCity's prevailing medical theories.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: As the saying goes, prevention is better than cure. Best not to wait until the illness becomes untreatable...
As Wuhuanzi rattles off an incomprehensible stream of medical terms, you feel like she's practically writing your epitaph already.

You've interrogated many Sinners before, and plenty tried to dodge questions with sweet talk and tall tales. But this is the first time someone has tried to distract you with an entire medical lecture.
She still sounds like that concerned young healer you know, but unlike during the fete incident, there's no real risk of Qi depletion for you anymore.
If not for your extensive interrogation experience, her elaborate medical discourse might have successfully diverted you from the matter at hand.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Thanks for the Eastian medicine crash course. Let's set that aside for now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Pay careful attention to my following questions. Your answers to them will determine the level of supervision you'll be placed under.
With the medical discussion over, Wuhuanzi reverts to her usual gloomy self. She adjusts her clothes and shrinks back into her chair.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why were you at the fete when the Wisteria Mania broke out?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Because of my bad luck.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Sigh... I wish I knew. I tried so hard to avoid that storyteller. When she went left, I went right. But somehow, no matter which direction I took, all paths led to the same place. I still ended up getting dragged into her story.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: And this time it was even worse. Dreams piled on top of illusions, and I ended up in that bizarre fete. Not only did I nearly die, but now I'm locked up in this... Bureau, or whatever it is.
As Wuhuanzi hangs her head in dejection, you find yourself feeling sympathy for her. Here's another soul cursed with the same awful luck as you.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Don't look at me with such pity. I've grown accustomed to walking hand in hand with misfortune. It's simply something I have to live with.
Her melancholy lasts but a moment before she regains her serene composure. You avert your gaze.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What brought you to DisCity?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: To save lives, of course.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What I mean is, you're from the Healer Vale in Eastia. Why travel all the way to DisCity to practice medicine? Weren't there enough patients back in Eastia?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I'm merely an herbalist. Traveling to heal the sick is my calling and how I gain experience. With Mania running rampant in DisCity, there are naturally more patients here, and thus, more opportunities to earn good karma.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You say you practice medicine for <color=#fb9259>good karma</color>. What exactly does it mean?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: It's part of the spiritual cultivation practice. Accumulating good karma lessens karmic burden, wards off misfortune, and enhances one's spiritual power and enlightenment.
What's karmic burden? Spiritual power and enlightenment? Now there are even more terms that are unheard-of.
Seeing your bewildered expression, Wuhuanzi realizes it's useless to pull you further into this cycle of incomprehension.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...Let's just say healing people earns me good karma.
According to Wuhuanzi, healing people earns her good karma. Does she mean that good karma is her only motivation for helping others, or is it a byproduct of her charitable acts?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've known other Sinners who were doctors. They acted out of professional calling, never mentioning any personal gain from helping others.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Even considering regional differences and varying medical philosophies, could practitioners of the same profession really have such contrasting motivations?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are your persistent attempts to treat me also about earning good karma?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Yes. And... since you're someone important around here, your life is worth even more good karma.
Wuhuanzi adds seriously as if she's trying to sound more convincing. You're not sure if you should be glad to hear about your high karmic value.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did I ever reveal that I was someone important during the fete?
Wuhuanzi mumbles something incoherent without giving a proper explanation. Seeing her evasiveness, you press on with your questions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But you've also helped ordinary citizens and people from the Drifter Camp. They're hardly what you'd call important people.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...In Eastia, we also believe having something is better than having nothing.
She fumbles with her words before finally forcing out a reasonable-sounding answer.
You let out a sigh, having expected her to say something more compassionate, like wanting to help patients recover or that she's unable to ignore others' suffering.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So according to what you're saying, you earn different amounts of good karma depending on who you save. Do you lose karma if you fail to treat them? How many ordinary citizens would equal one VIP? Is there a formula for this?
Your rapid-fire questions visibly unsettle Wuhuanzi, though she manages to maintain her composure.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...The mechanism behind is not meant to be understood by mere mortals like us.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So does practicing without a license reduce your good karma?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I merely lack DisCity's official permission. That doesn't affect my ability to heal patients.
Wuhuanzi deliberately sidesteps any questions about how karma is calculated, brushing them aside with vague answers.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can understand people's desire to accumulate wealth, but what's your purpose in accumulating good karma? Your belief seems to lack any support from concrete theory or data.
After a long silence, Wuhuanzi finally speaks, her voice barely above a whisper.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: To... break free from my curse of misfortune.
Out of all the things Wuhuanzi has said, two concepts appear more frequently than others: good karma and misfortune. They seem to form an impregnable barrier around her, like a looming shadow.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How much good karma do you need to break the curse? Um... Is there some kind of progress bar to track it?
Wuhuanzi shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: The ancient texts say: Three good deeds a day for three years shall bring heaven's blessing. Since my misfortune persists, I must not have accumulated enough good karma yet.
This baffles you a little. Would anyone really keep at something when absolutely no results can be seen?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Help me understand something. As a physician, when you prescribe medicine, don't you adjust the treatment plan based on how the patient responds?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, going back to our subject... If your actions aren't bringing any changes to your life, could it be that good karma simply isn't the right medicine for breaking your curse?
Wuhuanzi lifts her head slightly as if to speak, but after a moment, she drops her gaze again, fidgeting nervously with her fingers.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What I mean is, you've accumulated so much good karma already, and yet you still seem constantly troubled by bad luck...
Before you can finish speaking, you feel a surge of depressive energy coursing through the shackles. At the same time, you realize you might have just said exactly the wrong thing.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...You're right. I've tried so hard to accumulate good karma, so why am I still cursed with such terrible luck?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: A disaster destroyed my homeland and took my family away. I lost everything that mattered to me, only to end up cursed with this endless misfortune.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I don't know how much good karma is considered enough. I can only keep trying to earn more... Surely one day I'll have enough to break this curse, right?
Instead of deflecting with her usual mystical theories, Wuhuanzi opens up about her past in Eastia. Her last words sound less like a question and more like a quiet confession to herself.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: What good would knowing the truth do? Nothing can be changed... It would only bring more pain...
Her head sinks lower and lower as waves of despair seem to materialize around her, dark energy gathering and wrapping her in an ever-deeper darkness.
The shackles help bring Wuhuanzi back to her senses. You give her shoulder a gentle pat, pause the interrogation, and offer her a glass of water.
Good karma. You pick up your pen and write down this unfamiliar Eastian term.
Could something so intangible truly exist? Could accumulating good karma really break the curse of misfortune that plagues Wuhuanzi?
What makes her believe so firmly in this? Has she witnessed the miraculous power of good karma firsthand? Or is she simply chasing after some vague Eastian myth?
As the interrogation progresses, instead of finding answers, you're left with even more mysteries, ones that seem impossible to solve.
You set down your pen, having come to a decision.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That concludes this interrogation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Bureau has been monitoring and examining the conditions of your patients, and turns out they're all in good health. Though you may be practicing without a license, you are, without doubt, a qualified physician.
At your words, Wuhuanzi's tensed body begins to unfurl. She glances at you, and finding no trace of mockery in your expression, finally lets out a deep breath of relief.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Many people at the Bureau need medical attention. While we do have our own infirmary, I suppose we could give Eastian medicine a try.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course, our infirmary will monitor the progress. If you need anything, you can always reach out to Nightingale.
Wuhuanzi is taken aback. Not only have you stopped questioning her, but you've even permitted her unauthorized practice. Her usually expressionless face shows a mixture of disbelief and astonishment.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...Thank you. So, um, I can go now?
You nod and watch quietly as Wuhuanzi makes her way out of the interrogation room.
You try to organize your thoughts, setting aside for now your questions about good karma and misfortune.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If we consider good karma as a kind of currency, Wuhuanzi's practice isn't much different from regular medical care. Sometimes she even offers free treatment, not receiving any actual payment at all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...How is this any different from charity work?
Earlier, you had the impression she only cared about the number of patients she treated, not the actual results of her treatment.
But just now when she heard about her patients' excellent health, her visible relief was unmistakable. She didn't look like a doctor who would simply neglect her patients' conditions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Does she not want people to see her work as acts of kindness? Or maybe she's even trying to hide how much she truly cares about saving lives?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then... could she be using good karma as an excuse to hide her true feelings? Do people like her really exist? But why?
Try as you might, you can't make sense of it. Wuhuanzi is a web of contradictions, and her true motives remain frustratingly unclear.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: During today's interrogation, she kept dancing around my questions. Maybe she was also aware that her explanations didn't hold water, but just couldn't bring herself to admit it?
This guess seems a bit far-fetched even to you, but without more information, you can't come to any other conclusions.
She helped you in the illusion, and now you want to return the favor. Even if you can't break her so-called curse of misfortune, at least you might help her understand her true feelings.

A dull headache throbs in your temples as Wuhuanzi's cryptic Eastian incantations echo in your mind. You grab your pen again, drawing circles around the term good karma before adding a large question mark beside it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It looks like it all comes back to good karma in the end.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sigh... One step at a time.
